title: Native Weil compactification models under proper refinement
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the native abelian Weil categories $\mathcal W_S$, their ordinary derived categories, bounded constructible full subcategories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(S)$, and actual equivariant operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $h:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. A compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,r:\overline X\to Y)$ means a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and a proper map with $rj=h$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_c=Rr_*J_j$, with $J_j$ termwise native extension by zero. For compactifications $c_1,c_2$ and any proper $Y$-map $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with $vj_1=j_2$, there are natural isomorphisms on $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$
$$J_{j_2}\cong Rv_*J_{j_1},\qquad
F_{c_2}\cong Rr_{2*}Rv_*J_{j_1}\cong R(r_2v)_*J_{j_1}=F_{c_1}.$$
Moreover, for any two compactifications there exists a natural isomorphism $F_{c_2}\cong F_{c_1}$ as functors $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)\to D(\mathcal W_Y)$; in particular every $F_c$ is naturally isomorphic to the framework's chosen model $Rh_{0!}$. All components and inverses lie in the native equivariant derived categories. Absolute separatedness over $k_0$ is not assumed; no independence of these isomorphisms from refinement choices or cocycle assertion is part of the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, compactification calculation; agent adaptation to the native category of def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework, not a claim that the torsion etale Stacks statement proves the native coefficient case.

proof.text: All the compactification ambient schemes are finite type over $k_0$: each $r_i$ is finite type by the definition of proper, and its composite with the finite-type structure map of $Y$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Thus the native operations in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] apply to $X,\overline X_i,Y$. The open immersions $j_i$ are quasi-compact by the compactification hypotheses. In particular [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons](b) supplies their termwise derived functors $J_{j_i}$ on the bounded constructible source, and (a) supplies the identity and composite direct-image comparisons. None of these statements requires absolute separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined, setup; native operations supplied by the cited framework and basic comparisons

proof.text: For the given proper refinement $v$, take the square with top edge $j_1:X\to\overline X_1$, bottom edge $j_2:X\to\overline X_2$, left edge $\operatorname{id}_X$, and right edge $v$. Its commutativity is exactly $vj_1=j_2$. The identity is proper directly from the definition (its diagonal is an isomorphism, it is finite type, and every base change is an identity, hence closed); $v$ is proper by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sf-native-weil-open-proper-interchange] to this square. It gives $J_{j_2}R(\operatorname{id}_X)_*\cong Rv_*J_{j_1}$ on $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$. Compose with the inverse of $J_{j_2}$ whiskered with the identity-direct-image comparison of [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons](a) to obtain $\alpha_v:J_{j_2}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_*J_{j_1}$. The interchange lemma explicitly permits a non-Cartesian square, so no assertion that $v^{-1}(j_2X)=j_1X$ has entered the argument.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open) and 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), refinement square; native version is the cited interchange node

proof.text: Apply the functor $Rr_{2*}$ to $\alpha_v$ and use [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons](a), with $u=v$ and the second map $r_2$, in the inverse direction. This gives natural isomorphisms $F_{c_2}=Rr_{2*}J_{j_2}\cong Rr_{2*}Rv_*J_{j_1}\cong R(r_2v)_*J_{j_1}=Rr_{1*}J_{j_1}=F_{c_1}$, since $v$ is a $Y$-map. Explicitly the first arrow has component $Rr_{2*}(\alpha_v(K))$, with inverse $Rr_{2*}(\alpha_v(K)^{-1})$; the second arrow is the composite-direct-image comparison evaluated at $J_{j_1}K$. Hence the two displayed isomorphisms are natural in $K$. The composite-direct-image comparison holds on the entire native derived category, so no extra boundedness or constructibility of $Rv_*J_{j_1}K$ is required here.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined, displayed comparison along a morphism of compactifications

proof.text: For arbitrary $c_1,c_2$, apply [prop-nagata-compactification-category](i) with base $S=Y$ and morphism $h$. Its hypotheses are precisely the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $Y$ and the separated finite-type property of $h$. It supplies a compactification $d$ and proper $Y$-refinements $w_i:d\to c_i$. Apply the preceding refinement calculation to obtain natural isomorphisms $\gamma_i:F_{c_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_d$. Then $\gamma_1^{-1}\circ\gamma_2:F_{c_2}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_1}$ is the required comparison. Taking $c_1$ to be the framework's chosen Nagata compactification $(a,p)$ identifies $F_{c_1}$ with $Rh_{0!}$ by [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. This choice is a compactification in the present sense: $p$ is proper over $Y$, and its open immersion $a$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] applied to the triangle $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, since $pa=h$ is quasi-compact (finite type) and $p$ is separated, hence quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] (its diagonal is a closed immersion, which is affine and so quasi-compact). Every arrow used above and its inverse is already a native equivariant derived morphism by the cited basic comparisons and interchange lemma; applying native functors, composing and inverting preserves that property. This constructs an isomorphism for each choice of common refinement and makes no independence or cocycle claim.
